children.title: Lucid Dreaming Verified by Volitional Communication During REM Sleep (LaBerge, S., et al. 1981)

children.description: Reviewed various lucid dream induction techniques, finding MILD, WBTB, and external stimuli (light & sound cues) to be the most effective.

children.title: Neural Correlates of Dream Lucidity (Dresler et al., 2012)
children.description: fMRI and EEG research identified increased prefrontal cortex activity during lucid dreams, linking metacognition to lucidity.

children.title: Metacognitive Mechanisms Underlying Lucid Dreaming (Filevich, E., Dresler, M., et al. 2015)
children.description: Showed that lucid dreamers exhibit superior metacognitive abilities in wakefulness, particularly in self-awareness and cognitive control.

children.title: The Cognitive Neuroscience of Lucid Dreaming (Baird, B., et al. 2018)
children.description: Reviewed neuroscientific literature on lucid dreaming, suggesting links between lucid dreaming and real-world cognitive benefits.

children.title: Targeted Lucidity Reactivation During REM Sleep Using Real-Time Sleep Spindles Detection (Carr, M., et al. 2020)
children.description: Developed an open-source iOS/watchOS application to perform targeted lucidity reactivation, facilitating the testing of this method in various settings.

children.title: Real-Time Dialogue Between Experimenters and Dreamers During REM Sleep (Konkoly, K. R., et al. 2021)
children.description: Demonstrated that real-time communication with lucid dreamers is possible via eye movements and facial muscle signals.

children.title: Two-Way Communication in Lucid REM Sleep Dreaming (Baird, B., LaBerge, S., et al. 2021)
children.description: investigated the feasibility of establishing real-time, bidirectional communication with individuals during lucid REM sleep.

children.title: Highly effective verified lucid dream induction using combined cognitive-sensory training and wearable EEG: a multi-centre study (Carr, M., et al. 2024)
children.description: Demonstrated that combining SSILD-based cognitive training with targeted lucidity reactivation (TLR) and multimodal sensory cues during REM sleep, facilitated by wearable EEG technology, can effectively induce lucid dreams in a laboratory environment.

children.title: Provoking lucid dreams at home with sensory cues paired with pre-sleep cognitive training (Whitmore, N., et al. 2024)
children.description: Found that targeted lucidity reactivation (TLR) significantly increased the frequency of lucid dreams among participants, demonstrating that TLR can be effectively implemented with minimal technical requirements outside of a laboratory setting.
